title: Barchester Towers

meter_and_prosody: Prose. Prose fiction of common life: the continuous chaptered narrative, the full reported dialogue, the exact material description of rooms, clothes, money and work, and the slow accumulation of consequence. The author's characteristic manner is long, syntactically suspended sentences with delayed qualification.
historical_context: The 1900s: the London and Venetian society of the international set, and the American fortune in Europe. The record dates the work as composed between 1901 and 1902 and first published in 1902 and the corpus places it within American Realism and the Howells Program; Aestheticism and the Decadent Decade, it is catalogued under realist novel of common life; new woman and marriage-question novel.
literary_significance: The Wings of the Dove is the finest of James's late novels and the central text of the modern novel of moral ambiguity: its treatment of money, illness and the corruption of love made it the model for the twentieth-century novel of consciousness, and Milly Theale is one of the most memorable heroines in American fiction.
attribution_notes: Attribution is secure: the work was published under the author's name, also recorded as Henry James, Jr. No competing attribution or spurious edition is recorded for this title. The work is catalogued here as secondary canon.
bibliographical_notes: Published by Charles Scribner's Sons in New York in August 1902 and by Methuen in London in September 1902; the novel was begun in 1897 and laid aside before completion. The record grades the work as secondary canon.
